version.changelog:
medical-record-structurer 1.0.2 introduces explicit user-based billing and more detailed payment configuration.

- Added user_id parameter support to process_record API for per-user billing and balance checking.
- Updated payment integration details: includes SkillPay provider, price, chain, and skill ID information in config and documentation.
- Enhanced example code and CLI usage to demonstrate how to handle insufficient balance and provide recharge links.
- Clarified configuration and usage instructions in SKILL.md.

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its stated purpose (local EMR structuring with pay-per-use billing) but contains inconsistencies and extra artifacts (missing declared env var, a hard-coded API key in documentation, and an external upload script) that warrant caution before installation or use with real patient data.

dimensions.detail: The code and docs implement a local medical-record structurer and a SkillPay billing integration, which fits the skill name and description. However the registry metadata declares no required environment variables while the SKILL.md and scripts clearly rely on SKILLPAY_API_KEY; this mismatch is incoherent and should be corrected. The included Clawhub upload script is unrelated to runtime processing and is an extra capability (publishing the skill) that users may not expect.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructions focus on processing records and setting SKILLPAY_API_KEY, which is appropriate. The processing implementation shown is primarily local regex extraction. I could not review the truncated remainder of scripts/process_record.py — the visible parts do not transmit medical records to other endpoints except for billing calls to skillpay.me; confirm the truncated portion does not send PHI to third parties. The upload-to-clawhub.sh script would transmit a skill bundle to an external service if run; that script is not part of normal processing but increases the skill's attack surface if invoked.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided; this is an instruction-only skill with included scripts. Nothing is automatically downloaded or written during installation. That keeps install risk low, but included scripts contain network upload commands that would run only if explicitly executed by the user.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires a billing API key (SKILLPAY_API_KEY) to function, which is proportionate to its pay-per-use design — but the registry metadata lists no required env vars, creating a mismatch. More concerning: references/skillpay-api.md contains a long API-like string embedded in an example JSON body ('sk_7c3606...'), which looks like a real secret or a convincing placeholder; hardcoded example credentials in docs are risky and confusing. The upload script requires a Clawhub API token if used; that is unrelated to processing medical text and increases credential burden.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not modify system-wide agent settings in the visible files. The upload script references a fixed path (/home/node/.openclaw/workspace/skills/...), which assumes a particular environment but does not by itself change privileges. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal for skills).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement a local regex-based EMR structuring tool with pay-per-use billing. Before installing or using it: (1) Treat it as untrusted: do not process real patient/PHI until you have vetted the full code (the process_record.py file is truncated in the package listing — review the remainder to ensure no hidden exfiltration). (2) Correct the metadata mismatch: the registry should declare SKILLPAY_API_KEY as required; if you rely on automated checks, missing declarations are a red flag. (3) Remove or replace any hard-coded API keys in documentation/examples; that string in references/skillpay-api.md should be treated as sensitive or a poor placeholder. (4) The upload-to-clawhub.sh script can publish the skill to an external service — only run it if you control the target account and understand what it will upload. (5) If you will process real patient data, require code review and legal/IT approval (PHI handling); prefer using ephemeral test data and a rotated API key scoped to billing only. (6) If you want higher assurance, ask the author for: full, untruncated source; clarification on what data (if any) is sent to external services besides billing; and an explicit list of required environment variables and network endpoints.
